findings.title: The new t==nil guard reports that a nested vector element has "no Go type", and the new…
findings.claim: The new t==nil guard reports that a nested vector element has "no Go type", and the new test pins that message. But the failure comes from helpers.go storing the inner VectorType's custom name as just the bare prefix, so asVectorType/goType cannot resolve it. Nested vectors do have a Go type: the same test decodes them into [][]float32.

findings.title: makeNestedVectorType gives the inner vector a full `VectorType(<sub>, N)` custom string,…
findings.claim: makeNestedVectorType gives the inner vector a full `VectorType(<sub>, N)` custom string, but the production parser gives inner nested vectors the bare prefix. The fixture therefore models a type the wire never produces.

findings.title: TestUnmarshalVectorAcceptsWellFormedPayloads includes a 'payload with a trailing byte'…
findings.claim: TestUnmarshalVectorAcceptsWellFormedPayloads includes a 'payload with a trailing byte' case: a 13-byte int vector with 3 dimensions. That payload is malformed, yet the test asserts it decodes without error. The float fast paths reject any length other than Dimensions*size.

findings.title: The new comment says every path below turns Dimensions into an allocation
findings.claim: The new comment says every path below turns Dimensions into an allocation. The array destination path allocates nothing, and the PR's own test comment says so.

findings.title: The getCassandraLongType change is not limited to vectors
findings.claim: The getCassandraLongType change is not limited to vectors. Every unknown type nested in a list, set, map, tuple, UDT, frozen type or vector now keeps its class name as the custom name. No test checks getCassandraLongType directly.

findings.title: The new makeVectorType helper duplicates the existing makeDoubleVectorType and…
findings.claim: The new makeVectorType helper duplicates the existing makeDoubleVectorType and makeFloat32VectorType builders in the same file instead of replacing them.

findings.title: Commits do not follow CONTRIBUTING
findings.claim: Commits do not follow CONTRIBUTING.md's commit-message format: the subjects start lowercase with a conventional-commit prefix, and neither commit has the required `Patch by <authors>; reviewed by <Reviewers> for #####` line.

findings.title: A notable behaviour change ships without the CHANGELOG/godoc documentation CONTRIBUTING…
findings.claim: A notable behaviour change ships without the CHANGELOG/godoc documentation CONTRIBUTING requires: unknown custom type names now keep their name, and vectors are newly rejected on dimension bounds and on element types with no Go type.

findings.title: The same `info
findings.claim: The same `info.Dimensions > 0 && data != nil` guard appears twice in a row, opening two adjacent blocks.

findings.title: Overflow safety at the fast-path multiplication is implicit
findings.claim: Overflow safety at the fast-path multiplication is implicit. It depends on vectorFixedElemSize returning exactly 8 and 4 for double and float, and nothing at the multiplication site says so.

findings.title: Element-type classification is now spread over three parallel switches:…
findings.claim: Element-type classification is now spread over three parallel switches: vectorFixedElemSize, isVectorVariableLengthType, and the new vectorElemMinSize, which composes them and recurses on VectorType.

findings.title: The header comment describes `elemMin` and the bound above the negative-dimension check,…
findings.claim: The header comment describes `elemMin` and the bound above the negative-dimension check, apart from the block that defines elemMin. It also says 'unmarshalList does the same', but unmarshalList divides by a fixed 4 rather than an element minimum.

findings.title: getCassandraLongType now keeps an unknown type's name only in its final basic-type branch
findings.claim: getCassandraLongType now keeps an unknown type's name only in its final basic-type branch. Its sibling degrade-to-custom returns (map arity error, vector dimension parse error) still return NewNativeType(TypeCustom) with an empty name.

findings.title: makeVectorType duplicates the existing makeDoubleVectorType/makeFloat32VectorType (and…
findings.claim: makeVectorType duplicates the existing makeDoubleVectorType/makeFloat32VectorType (and vector_bench_test.go's makeFloatVectorType). It also takes the element as two separate values, a Type and a class-name string, that must agree.

findings.title: Test comments claim more than their assertions show
findings.claim: Test comments claim more than their assertions show. The 'pins the bound as non-narrowing' suite checks six sample shapes, and 'The concrete destinations pin that the guard narrowed nothing' covers a single concrete destination ([][]float32).

findings.title: vectorElemMinSize's saturation branch (`return math
findings.claim: vectorElemMinSize's saturation branch (`return math.MaxInt32`) has no test row, although the overflow handling is a stated purpose of the function.

findings.title: TestUnmarshalVectorRejectsNestedCountBeforeAllocating measures process-wide runtime
findings.claim: TestUnmarshalVectorRejectsNestedCountBeforeAllocating measures process-wide runtime.MemStats.TotalAlloc. Allocations by other goroutines in the unit test binary count against its 128 KiB threshold.

findings.title: The test comment says the overflow cases "use the word size so the wrap lands on a…
findings.claim: The test comment says the overflow cases "use the word size so the wrap lands on a 32-bit target too". On a 32-bit target, though, the unit-tagged gocql test package cannot compile, so that path is never built or run.

findings.title: The PR says "Every new test fails against pristine marshal
findings.claim: The PR says "Every new test fails against pristine marshal.go/helpers.go". Several new tests pass on the base behaviour, so this is false.

findings.title: TestUnmarshalVectorZeroDimensionsDoesNotTouchSubType and the guard comment say a zero…
findings.claim: TestUnmarshalVectorZeroDimensionsDoesNotTouchSubType and the guard comment say a zero VectorType with a nil SubType is safe at zero dimensions. That only holds for a concrete-slice destination: with an *any destination, unmarshalVector still calls info.Zero(), which dereferences the nil SubType.

findings.title: The headline behaviour change ("a short or zero-length non-NULL payload
findings.claim: The headline behaviour change ("a short or zero-length non-NULL payload ... now errors") has no test for the zero-length case. No test passes a non-nil empty payload with Dimensions > 0.

findings.title: getCassandraLongType now returns NativeType with `custom` set to the full class name for…
findings.claim: getCassandraLongType now returns NativeType with `custom` set to the full class name for every unrecognised type, not only vector elements. That changes the public TypeInfo.Custom() and String() output for collection, tuple, UDT and vector-subtype metadata across the driver, and neither the commit nor the PR body calls it a contract change.

findings.title: The new bound error 'unmarshal vector: %d dimensions do not fit in %d bytes' fires…
findings.claim: The new bound error 'unmarshal vector: %d dimensions do not fit in %d bytes' fires before the fast path's exact-length error. For a payload that is short but non-wrapping, the user-visible message changes from the precise expected byte count to a dimension-count message. Sibling decoders still report exact byte expectations.

findings.title: The new bound comment says unmarshalList "does the same", but unmarshalList uses a fixed…
findings.claim: The new bound comment says unmarshalList "does the same", but unmarshalList uses a fixed 4-byte floor, applies it only to slices, and checks after the size prefix. The vector bound uses a per-type recursive minimum and also covers arrays.

findings.title: The new comment says every path below turns Dimensions into an allocation, but the array…
findings.claim: The new comment says every path below turns Dimensions into an allocation, but the array path allocates nothing. The PR's own test comment says so.

findings.title: The *any destination in vectors is resolved through info
findings.claim: The *any destination in vectors is resolved through info.Zero(), which discards the NewWithError error, plus a new nil check. The sibling unmarshalList resolves the same thing through goType(info.Elem) and propagates its error. There are now two different classifiers for "element has a Go type".

findings.title: The new test fixtures makeVectorType/makeNestedVectorType copy the existing…
findings.claim: The new test fixtures makeVectorType/makeNestedVectorType copy the existing makeFloat32VectorType/makeDoubleVectorType bodies. makeVectorType takes the Type and the class name as independent arguments, so they can disagree. makeNestedVectorType gives the inner vector a fully qualified custom name, unlike the wire path (helpers.go:271), which stores only the bare prefix. A third builder, wireVectorType, builds the real shape.

findings.title: The new dimension bound runs before unmarshalVector validates the destination…
findings.claim: The new dimension bound runs before unmarshalVector validates the destination (non-pointer, non-empty interface, unsupported kind, array-length mismatch), so a short payload now reports "N dimensions do not fit in M bytes" instead of the caller's programming error.

findings.title: The new 'no Go type for element type %v' error renders a nested vector element as…
findings.claim: The new 'no Go type for element type %v' error renders a nested vector element as 'custom(org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.VectorType)', with no inner element type or dimension. That contradicts the PR's claim that the error now says which type the server sent.

findings.title: The new nil-Zero guard replaces the specific error that SubType
findings.claim: The new nil-Zero guard replaces the specific error that SubType.NewWithError produced (VectorType.Zero swallows it) with a generic string. The sibling unmarshalList surfaces its element-type error as 'unmarshal list: cannot determine element type: %v'.

findings.title: The PR body's 'Behaviour change' section omits that a NULL value for a vector with…
findings.claim: The PR body's 'Behaviour change' section omits that a NULL value for a vector with negative dimensions now returns an error. Previously it decoded to a nil slice with a nil error.

findings.title: Commit 0276a66's message says the bound relies on every element taking at least one byte
findings.claim: Commit 0276a66's message says the bound relies on every element taking at least one byte. The commit actually adds a recursive per-type minimum (vectorElemMinSize), so the message misdescribes the mechanism it introduces.

findings.title: A zero-dimensional VectorType with a nil SubType still panics when unmarshaled into…
findings.claim: A zero-dimensional VectorType with a nil SubType still panics when unmarshaled into *any, despite the new test and comment claiming the subtype is untouched.

findings.title: The comment saying unmarshalList uses the same bound is inaccurate: lists use a fixed…
findings.claim: The comment saying unmarshalList uses the same bound is inaccurate: lists use a fixed length-prefix floor, whereas vectors use a recursive type-dependent minimum and cover different destination paths.

findings.title: makeVectorType accepts the logical element Type and its Cassandra class-name suffix…
findings.claim: makeVectorType accepts the logical element Type and its Cassandra class-name suffix independently, allowing internally contradictory fixtures.

findings.title: The overflow-saturation branch in vectorElemMinSize is unprotected by a test case
findings.claim: The overflow-saturation branch in vectorElemMinSize is unprotected by a test case.

findings.title: The allocation-regression test uses process-wide TotalAlloc and can be polluted by…
findings.claim: The allocation-regression test uses process-wide TotalAlloc and can be polluted by allocations from unrelated background goroutines.

findings.title: The test comment claims its word-size expressions exercise wrapping on 32-bit targets,…
findings.claim: The test comment claims its word-size expressions exercise wrapping on 32-bit targets, but the unit test package cannot compile there because another unit test compares an int with math.MaxUint32.

findings.title: The PR statement that every new test fails on the pristine implementation is false
findings.claim: The PR statement that every new test fails on the pristine implementation is false.

findings.title: The advertised rejection of a zero-length non-NULL payload with positive dimensions has…
findings.claim: The advertised rejection of a zero-length non-NULL payload with positive dimensions has no direct regression test.

findings.title: Preserving every unknown class name changes the public TypeInfo
findings.claim: Preserving every unknown class name changes the public TypeInfo.Custom() and String() results for all metadata callers, not only vector error diagnostics.

findings.title: The new payload bound runs before destination validation and can replace a…
findings.claim: The new payload bound runs before destination validation and can replace a caller-programming error with a payload-size diagnosis.

findings.title: Unknown-name preservation is inconsistent across parser fallback branches: the new…
findings.claim: Unknown-name preservation is inconsistent across parser fallback branches: the new basic-type fallback retains the name, while malformed map and vector fallbacks still return unnamed custom types.
